why: devā́s tvā dadhiré puráḥ is grammatical; devānām would not fit the syntax.
Pada-initial prathamám has all pre-udatta syllables marked anudatta; the marking is correct at verse start.
dāśúṣo nṝ́n (genitive before nṝn) is the right form; dāśuṣe would not construe.
ubhé aprā ródasī is sound (aprā = filled); metre fine.
akṣāḥ (aorist of akṣ, flowed) matches the preceding verse's akṣāḥ; correct.
Devāpi is a proper name (the hymn's seer); not a typo.
ukṣitáḥ (sprinkled, grown) is a regular participle; sense and metre fit.
ā́ bhúvaḥ is a correct injunctive form; nothing wrong.
ahám huve (I invoke) is the expected verb; fine.
mádyāya (for the intoxicating one) is a genuine adjective form, accent consistent.
sákhā + átho sandhi gives sákhātho; the accent marks match that merger.
javás-e (for speed) suits yunajmi; jīvase would not.
visṛ́taḥ (flowing apart) is grammatical and fits the river context.
yajatra (vocative, O adorable one) is a regular Agni epithet.
kác cid ā́ is a normal indefinite phrase; nothing broken.
mánase (dative, for the mind) parallels várāya; correct.
yā́d evá vidmá (as far as we know) is sound sandhi of yāt + eva.
ánv apā́ṃ khā́ni is the regular anu + apām; fine.
stómasya vardhanā (increasers of the hymn) is a coherent reading; no error.
viśvápsu (all-formed) is a known compound; accent fine.
marúdbhyo vāyáve (datives) parallel devébhyaḥ; correct.
néd evá mā yunájan (lest they yoke me) is sound.
marúdbhiḥ with final visarga to ī before r is regular sandhi.
índram asya rāyáḥ (accusative plus genitive) is the right construction with īmahe.
dadṛśe (perfect, was seen) is correct; metre fine.
prá índrasya with pra elided after vowel; correct sandhi.
dṛśé víśvāya sū́ryam (for all to see) is sound.
ápāṃsi (works) is a regular neuter plural.
subhárā (well-laden) is a known adjective; fits rátham.
suvī́ryaiḥ (instrumental plural) parallels rāyā́; correct.
savitrā́ is the instrumental of Savitṛ, parallel to ādityaiḥ, parvatebhiḥ.
vaktvā́ni (things to be said) recurs in the following line; genuine.
víśvāsām (genitive plural feminine) agrees with purā́m; correct.
ávasi (you favour) is a regular verb; fine.
árṇāṃsi (floods) is a regular neuter plural; sense fits.
suvī́ryā (neuter plural) fits the question; correct.
víśvās te spṛ́dhaḥ (all your rivals) is sound sandhi.
Pada-initial pṛthivyā́ has all pre-udatta syllables marked anudatta; correct.
váhāni (subjunctive, may I bring) is correct.
kravíṣā (raw flesh) fits the context of sorcerers and horse/cattle flesh.
karathaḥ (you two do) is a regular dual verb with rājānā.
deṣṇásya (of the gift) is a genuine noun; correct.
yuvasva (join) is the correct imperative here.
deváś ca savitā́ bhágaḥ is a normal list with ca; fine.
śivásya (of the kindly one) is a regular adjective; fine.
índra ihá merges to indreha; regular sandhi.
barhír u (with particle u) is sound; metre fine.
gotrā́ṇi (cow-pens) fits the cattle context of the neighbouring lines.
savā́saḥ (impulses) echoes savāya in the preceding verse; correct.
yám átra (whom here) is sound; fine.
dātrā́ṇi (gifts) is a regular neuter plural.
barhíṣaḥ (genitive) with sā́nau is fine.

suggest: त्वं नो॑ अग्ने॒ महो॑भिः पा॒हि विश्व॑स्या॒ अरा॑तेः । उ॒त द्वि॒षो मर्त्य॑स्य ॥
why: Line starts with a svarita-marked नो॑ with no preceding udatta and the first pada is one syllable short of gayatri, so the opening word (त्वं) was dropped.
sáhasvatī (powerful, dual) continues the sah- wordplay of the verse; correct.
yád átra (when here) is sound; fine.
hárasvatī (full of fury) suits ducchúnā; correct.
Pada-initial prathamā́ has pre-udatta syllables marked anudatta; correct.
yahvásya (of the youthful one, Agni) is a regular epithet.
bráhmaṇi (locative) parallels sóme, stóme, ukthé; correct.
yajñáś ca bhūd (and the sacrifice became) is regular sandhi; fine.
